text:
sana: Morning — nightly evals flagged a big perplexity/f1 regression on the long-context prompt set for model 'redwood-cassiopea-7b' under int8 quant. See summary below.


eval-bot: nightly-evals: redwood-cassiopea-7b int8 run failed 2026-03-18 03:12Z. Metric: perplexity +38% vs baseline; timeout rate 6% (was 0.6%). Full report: https://redwood-infra/reports/nightly/1965432100


sana: Attached snippet from harness logs:
```
worker-42 | eval: starting example 0
worker-42 | sample: generation took 12.3s
worker-42 | ERROR: sample timed out after 10s
worker-42 | exit_code=137
```


oliver: 137 suggests OOM/killed. But timeouts too. Are these the same examples that blow up on sequence length? Could be KV cache growth with long contexts + int8 kernel memory behavior.


maya: Was there any quantizer change yesterday? CI shows a tiny int8 packing tweak landed (commit 9f3a). @nikhil did we roll that to the eval cluster?


nikhil: yep, 9f3a went to prod in the quantizer package on 03/17 22:40Z. We also had the autoscaler restart a few nodes at 02:58Z due to kernel panic on a GPU host — I can pull kube events.


nikhil: kube events snippet:
```
Node/gpu-node-17 condition: KernelPanic
pod/runner-1234 evicted
pod/runner-1256 killed (OOMKilled)
```


maya: If nodes were being recycled, the harness's worker pool can lose warm cache and trigger longer generations; int8 kernels may fallback to slower code-paths if memory shapes mismatch. Might explain both perf regression and higher timeout rate.


sana: I reran the failing example locally on a stable node without the quantizer patch and int8 config; baseline throughput ~ 180 tok/s. With int8+9f3a I see 95 tok/s and occasional huge memory spikes.


oliver: Can you paste the exact eval command and the model config you're using? Also paste the tokenizer version.


sana: Command:
```
EVAL_ENV=nightly MODEL=redwood-cassiopea-7b QUANT=INT8 ./scripts/run_eval.sh --prompt-set long_context --timeout 10
```
Model config: quant_scheme=int8_pack, kv_cache=true, tokenizer=tokenizer-v2.1


maya: Try forcing KV cache disabled (kv_cache=false) to see if perf stabilizes. Also re-run with QUANT=FP16 to see if it's quant-specific.


sana: Quick results:
- fp16 run: no perf regression, perplexity baseline.
- int8 with kv_cache=false: timeout rate dropped to 0.9%, perf improved to 160 tok/s
- int8 with kv_cache=true: 6% timeouts, tok/s 92


nikhil: That strongly points to int8+kv cache interaction. I can roll back 9f3a from the quantizer package on the eval fleet for a canary test.


oliver: Can we also get a small reproducer snippet (single prompt) that triggers the spike so we can run CPU-profiling? Also add `RW_DEBUG_MEM=1` env to dump allocator stats.


sana: Will add repro to GH issue: https://github.com/redwood-inference/infra/issues/4321 (short repro + logs + failing example). Attaching sample prompt and minimal run script.


maya: Good. If rollback fixes it, we need a regression test in the harness to cover long_context + int8 + kv_cache toggles.


infra-bot: Scheduled maintenance: kernel updates rolled 03/17 02:55-03:05Z affecting gpu-node-15..18


sana: Thanks all — I'll track the canary rollback and post results here. :thumbsup:
